# Merge duplicate shops (map higher ID to lower ID)
shop_id_mapping = {57: 0, 58: 1, 11: 10, 40: 39}
sales_train["shop_id"] = sales_train["shop_id"].replace(shop_id_mapping)
print(f"Unique shops after merge: {sales_train['shop_id'].nunique()}")

Unique shops after merge: 56

Remove outliers from item_price and item_cnt_day before aggregation

In [261]:
# Remove outliers using IQR method
print(f"Before outlier removal: {len(sales_train):,} rows")

# Remove negative prices and extremely high prices (> 99.9th percentile)
price_upper = sales_train["item_price"].quantile(0.99)
price_mask = (sales_train["item_price"] > 0) & (sales_train["item_price"] <= price_upper)

# Remove negative counts and extremely high daily counts (> 99.9th percentile)
cnt_upper = sales_train["item_cnt_day"].quantile(0.99)
cnt_mask = (sales_train["item_cnt_day"] >= 0) & (sales_train["item_cnt_day"] <= cnt_upper)

sales_train = sales_train[price_mask & cnt_mask]
print(f"After outlier removal: {len(sales_train):,} rows")
print(f"Removed: {(~price_mask).sum() + (~cnt_mask).sum():,} outliers")
print(f"Price range: [{sales_train['item_price'].min():.2f}, {sales_train['item_price'].max():.2f}]")
print(f"Count range: [{sales_train['item_cnt_day'].min()}, {sales_train['item_cnt_day'].max()}]")

Before outlier removal: 2,935,849 rows
After outlier removal: 2,872,935 rows
Removed: 63,482 outliers
Price range: [0.07, 5999.00]
Count range: [1.0, 5.0]

Aggregate daily → monthly and create full matrix with all (shop, item, month) combinations

In [262]:
# Step 1: Aggregate daily sales to monthly
monthly_sales = (
    sales_train
    .groupby(["date_block_num", "shop_id", "item_id"])
    .agg(item_cnt_month=("item_cnt_day", "sum"), item_price_avg=("item_price", "mean"))
    .reset_index()
)
print(f"Monthly sales: {monthly_sales.shape[0]:,} rows")

Monthly sales: 1,592,043 rows
In [263]:
# Step 2: Create full matrix (all shop-item combinations per month)
matrix_parts = [
    pd.DataFrame(
        list(product([m], d["shop_id"].unique(), d["item_id"].unique())),
        columns=["date_block_num", "shop_id", "item_id"]
    )
    for m, d in monthly_sales.groupby("date_block_num")
]
matrix = pd.concat(matrix_parts, ignore_index=True)
print(f"Full matrix: {matrix.shape[0]:,} rows")

Full matrix: 10,721,984 rows
In [264]:

    .merge(monthly_sales, on=["date_block_num", "shop_id", "item_id"], how="left")
    .merge(items[["item_id", "item_category_id"]], on="item_id", how="left")
)
matrix["item_cnt_month"] = matrix["item_cnt_month"].fillna(0)

Fill missing item_price_avg with item's average price (then category average, then global average)

In [272]:
# Fill missing prices: item avg → category avg → global avg
matrix["item_price_avg"] = matrix["item_price_avg"].fillna(
    matrix.groupby("item_id")["item_price_avg"].transform("mean")
)
matrix["item_price_avg"] = matrix["item_price_avg"].fillna(
    matrix.groupby("item_category_id")["item_price_avg"].transform("mean")
)
matrix["item_price_avg"] = matrix["item_price_avg"].fillna(matrix["item_price_avg"].mean())
print(f"Missing item_price_avg: {matrix['item_price_avg'].isnull().sum()}")

In [273]:

matrix["month"] = matrix["date_block_num"] % 12
print(f"Added month feature (0-11 for seasonality)")

Lag features: sales from previous months (1, 2, 3, 6, 12)

In [274]:
lag_features = []
for lag in [1, 2, 3, 6, 12]:
    col = f"item_cnt_month_lag_{lag}"
    matrix[col] = matrix.groupby(["shop_id", "item_id"])["item_cnt_month"].shift(lag)
    lag_features.append(col)
print(f"Created {len(lag_features)} lag features")

Created 5 lag features

Trend/momentum features: lag differences to capture sales acceleration/deceleration

In [275]:
# Trend features: differences between consecutive lags
trend_features = []
matrix["trend_lag1_lag2"] = matrix["item_cnt_month_lag_1"] - matrix["item_cnt_month_lag_2"]
matrix["trend_lag2_lag3"] = matrix["item_cnt_month_lag_2"] - matrix["item_cnt_month_lag_3"]
trend_features = ["trend_lag1_lag2", "trend_lag2_lag3"]
print(f"Created {len(trend_features)} trend features")

Created 2 trend features

Rolling means: average of last 3 and 6 months

In [276]:
rolling_features = []
for window in [3, 6]:
    col = f"item_cnt_month_roll_mean_{window}"
    matrix[col] = matrix.groupby(["shop_id", "item_id"])["item_cnt_month"].transform(
        lambda x: x.shift(1).rolling(window, min_periods=1).mean()
    )
    rolling_features.append(col)
print(f"Created {len(rolling_features)} rolling features")

Created 2 rolling features

Mean encoding: expanding average by shop, item, category

In [277]:
# Mean encoding (expanding average to avoid data leakage)
mean_features = []
for group_cols in [["shop_id"], ["item_id"], ["item_category_id"], ["shop_id", "item_category_id"]]:
    col = f"item_cnt_month_{'_'.join(group_cols)}_avg"
    matrix[col] = matrix.groupby(group_cols)["item_cnt_month"].transform(
        lambda x: x.shift(1).expanding().mean()
    )
    mean_features.append(col)
print(f"Created {len(mean_features)} mean encoding features")

Created 4 mean encoding features

Recency features: first/last month item appeared, months since last sale

In [279]:
# Item first/last appearance in training (helps identify new vs established items)
item_first_month = matrix.groupby("item_id")["date_block_num"].transform("min")
item_last_month = matrix.groupby("item_id")["date_block_num"].transform("max")

matrix["item_first_month"] = item_first_month
matrix["item_age"] = matrix["date_block_num"] - item_first_month  # How long item has existed
matrix["months_since_item_last_sale"] = matrix["date_block_num"] - item_last_month.clip(upper=matrix["date_block_num"] - 1)

# Shop-item pair first appearance
shop_item_first = matrix.groupby(["shop_id", "item_id"])["date_block_num"].transform("min")
matrix["shop_item_first_month"] = shop_item_first
matrix["shop_item_age"] = matrix["date_block_num"] - shop_item_first

recency_features = ["item_age", "shop_item_age"]
print(f"Created {len(recency_features)} recency features")

Modeling¶

In [281]:
# Prepare training data - use only months >= 12 (recent data is more predictive)
MIN_TRAIN_MONTH = 12
matrix_train = matrix[matrix["date_block_num"] >= MIN_TRAIN_MONTH].copy()
print(f"Using months {MIN_TRAIN_MONTH}-33 for training (dropped early months with distribution shift)")

feature_cols = [
    "shop_id", "item_id", "item_category_id", "month", "item_price_avg",
    *lag_features, *trend_features, *rolling_features, *mean_features, *recency_features
]
X_train, y_train = matrix_train[feature_cols], matrix_train["item_cnt_month"]
print(f"Training: {X_train.shape[0]:,} rows, {len(feature_cols)} features")

Using months 12-33 for training (dropped early months with distribution shift)
Training: 6,275,726 rows, 20 features

# Scale features
scaler = StandardScaler()
X_train_scaled = scaler.fit_transform(X_train)

# Prepare test set now (needed for evaluate_model)
test_df = test.copy()

# CRITICAL FIX: Apply same shop_id mapping as training data!
test_df["shop_id"] = test_df["shop_id"].replace(shop_id_mapping)

test_df["date_block_num"] = 34
test_df["month"] = 34 % 12
test_df = test_df.merge(items[["item_id", "item_category_id"]], on="item_id", how="left")
test_df["item_category_id"] = test_df["item_category_id"].fillna(test_df["item_category_id"].mode()[0])

# Add features from training data
price_data = matrix[matrix["date_block_num"] == 33][["shop_id", "item_id", "item_price_avg"]].copy()
test_df = test_df.merge(price_data, on=["shop_id", "item_id"], how="left")

for lag in [1, 2, 3, 6, 12]:
    lag_data = matrix[matrix["date_block_num"] == 34 - lag][["shop_id", "item_id", "item_cnt_month"]].copy()
    lag_data.columns = ["shop_id", "item_id", f"item_cnt_month_lag_{lag}"]
    test_df = test_df.merge(lag_data, on=["shop_id", "item_id"], how="left")

# Trend features for test (computed from lags after fillna)
test_df["trend_lag1_lag2"] = test_df["item_cnt_month_lag_1"].fillna(0) - test_df["item_cnt_month_lag_2"].fillna(0)
test_df["trend_lag2_lag3"] = test_df["item_cnt_month_lag_2"].fillna(0) - test_df["item_cnt_month_lag_3"].fillna(0)

for window in [3, 6]:
    roll = matrix[matrix["date_block_num"].isin([33 - i for i in range(window)])].groupby(["shop_id", "item_id"])["item_cnt_month"].mean().reset_index()
    roll.columns = ["shop_id", "item_id", f"item_cnt_month_roll_mean_{window}"]
    test_df = test_df.merge(roll, on=["shop_id", "item_id"], how="left")

for cols in [["shop_id"], ["item_id"], ["item_category_id"], ["shop_id", "item_category_id"]]:
    enc = matrix.groupby(cols)["item_cnt_month"].mean().reset_index()
    enc.columns = [*cols, f"item_cnt_month_{'_'.join(cols)}_avg"]
    test_df = test_df.merge(enc, on=cols, how="left")

# Recency features for test (month 34)
item_stats = matrix.groupby("item_id")["date_block_num"].agg(["min", "max"]).reset_index()
item_stats.columns = ["item_id", "item_first_month", "item_last_month"]
test_df = test_df.merge(item_stats, on="item_id", how="left")
test_df["item_age"] = 34 - test_df["item_first_month"].fillna(34)

shop_item_stats = matrix.groupby(["shop_id", "item_id"])["date_block_num"].min().reset_index()
shop_item_stats.columns = ["shop_id", "item_id", "shop_item_first_month"]
test_df = test_df.merge(shop_item_stats, on=["shop_id", "item_id"], how="left")
test_df["shop_item_age"] = 34 - test_df["shop_item_first_month"].fillna(34)

# Drop intermediate columns
test_df = test_df.drop(columns=["item_first_month", "item_last_month", "shop_item_first_month"], errors="ignore")

test_df = test_df.fillna(0)
X_test_scaled = scaler.transform(test_df[feature_cols])

print(f"Train: {X_train_scaled.shape}, Test: {X_test_scaled.shape}")

Evaluation Function (same as bikes.ipynb)¶

In [283]:
def evaluate_model(model, model_name, X_train, y_train, X_test):
    """Train model, evaluate on train, and predict on test. Same as bikes.ipynb."""
    model.fit(X_train, y_train)
    
    y_pred_train = np.clip(model.predict(X_train), 0, 20)
    y_pred_test = np.clip(model.predict(X_test), 0, 20)
    
    train_rmse = np.sqrt(mean_squared_error(y_train, y_pred_train))
    
    fig, axes = plt.subplots(nrows=1, ncols=3, figsize=(18, 5))
    
    # Plot 1: Train actual vs predicted distribution
    # Sample for histogram (full data too large)
    sample_idx = np.random.choice(len(y_train), size=min(50000, len(y_train)), replace=False)
    sns.histplot(y_train.iloc[sample_idx], kde=True, ax=axes[0], label="Actual", color="blue", alpha=0.5)
    sns.histplot(y_pred_train[sample_idx], kde=True, ax=axes[0], label="Predicted", color="orange", alpha=0.5)
    axes[0].set_title(f"{model_name}: Train Distribution")
    axes[0].set_xlabel("item_cnt_month")
    axes[0].legend()
    
    # Plot 2: Train actual vs predicted scatter (sample for visibility)
    scatter_idx = np.random.choice(len(y_train), size=min(10000, len(y_train)), replace=False)
    axes[1].scatter(y_train.iloc[scatter_idx], y_pred_train[scatter_idx], alpha=0.3, s=10)
    axes[1].plot([0, 20], [0, 20], "r--", lw=2)
    axes[1].set_xlabel("Actual")
    axes[1].set_ylabel("Predicted")
    axes[1].set_title(f"{model_name}: Train Actual vs Predicted")
    
    # Plot 3: Test predictions distribution
    sns.histplot(y_pred_test, kde=True, ax=axes[2], color="green")
    axes[2].set_title(f"{model_name}: Test Predictions Distribution")
    axes[2].set_xlabel("Predicted item_cnt_month")
    
    plt.suptitle(f"{model_name} - Train RMSE: {train_rmse:.4f}", fontsize=14, fontweight="bold")
    plt.tight_layout()
    plt.show()
    
    return y_pred_train, y_pred_test, train_rmse

Random Forest (with Optuna)¶

In [287]:
# Use UNSCALED data for tree models + temporal validation split
# Validation = month 33 (closest to test month 34)
X_train_raw = X_train.values  # Unscaled!
X_test_raw = test_df[feature_cols].values

# Use matrix_train (months >= 12) for validation split
val_mask = matrix_train["date_block_num"] == 33
train_mask = (matrix_train["date_block_num"] >= MIN_TRAIN_MONTH) & (matrix_train["date_block_num"] < 33)

# Sample from training months only
sample_size = 500000
train_indices = np.where(train_mask)[0]
np.random.seed(42)
sample_idx = np.random.choice(train_indices, size=min(sample_size, len(train_indices)), replace=False)

X_tr = X_train_raw[sample_idx]
y_tr = y_train.iloc[sample_idx].values

# Validation = all of month 33
X_val = X_train_raw[val_mask.values]
y_val = y_train[val_mask].values

print(f"Optuna: train sample {len(X_tr):,}, val (month 33) {len(X_val):,}")

def rf_objective(trial):
    params = {
        "n_estimators": trial.suggest_int("n_estimators", 50, 150),
        "max_depth": trial.suggest_int("max_depth", 3, 10),  # Lower = less overfitting
        "min_samples_split": trial.suggest_int("min_samples_split", 5, 20),
        "min_samples_leaf": trial.suggest_int("min_samples_leaf", 5, 20),  # Higher = less overfitting
        "random_state": 42,
        "n_jobs": -1
    }
    model = RandomForestRegressor(**params)
    model.fit(X_tr, y_tr)
    pred = np.clip(model.predict(X_val), 0, 20)
    return np.sqrt(mean_squared_error(y_val, pred))

optuna.logging.set_verbosity(optuna.logging.WARNING)
rf_study = optuna.create_study(direction="minimize", sampler=TPESampler(seed=42))
rf_study.optimize(rf_objective, n_trials=30, show_progress_bar=True)

print(f"Best Random Forest params: {rf_study.best_params}")
print(f"Best Val RMSE: {rf_study.best_value:.4f}")

# Train Random Forest with best params on full UNSCALED data
rf_model = RandomForestRegressor(**rf_study.best_params, random_state=42, n_jobs=-1)
y_pred_train_rf, y_pred_test_rf, rmse_rf = evaluate_model(rf_model, "Random Forest", X_train_raw, y_train, X_test_raw)
















































XGBoost (with Optuna)¶


















In [289]:






# XGBoost with more regularization to prevent overfitting
def xgb_objective(trial):
    params = {
        "n_estimators": trial.suggest_int("n_estimators", 50, 200),
        "learning_rate": trial.suggest_float("learning_rate", 0.01, 0.2, log=True),
        "max_depth": trial.suggest_int("max_depth", 2, 6),  # Shallow trees!
        "min_child_weight": trial.suggest_int("min_child_weight", 10, 100),  # More regularization
        "subsample": trial.suggest_float("subsample", 0.6, 0.9),
        "colsample_bytree": trial.suggest_float("colsample_bytree", 0.6, 0.9),
        "reg_alpha": trial.suggest_float("reg_alpha", 0.1, 10, log=True),  # L1
        "reg_lambda": trial.suggest_float("reg_lambda", 0.1, 10, log=True),  # L2
        "random_state": 42,
        "n_jobs": -1
    }
    model = XGBRegressor(**params)
    model.fit(X_tr, y_tr)
    pred = np.clip(model.predict(X_val), 0, 20)
    return np.sqrt(mean_squared_error(y_val, pred))

xgb_study = optuna.create_study(direction="minimize", sampler=TPESampler(seed=42))
xgb_study.optimize(xgb_objective, n_trials=50, show_progress_bar=True)

print(f"Best XGBoost params: {xgb_study.best_params}")
print(f"Best Val RMSE: {xgb_study.best_value:.4f}")

LightGBM (with Optuna)¶


















In [291]:






# LightGBM with Optuna tuning
def lgbm_objective(trial):
    params = {
        "n_estimators": trial.suggest_int("n_estimators", 50, 300),
        "learning_rate": trial.suggest_float("learning_rate", 0.01, 0.2, log=True),
        "max_depth": trial.suggest_int("max_depth", 3, 8),
        "num_leaves": trial.suggest_int("num_leaves", 15, 127),
        "min_child_samples": trial.suggest_int("min_child_samples", 10, 100),
        "subsample": trial.suggest_float("subsample", 0.6, 0.95),
        "colsample_bytree": trial.suggest_float("colsample_bytree", 0.6, 0.95),
        "reg_alpha": trial.suggest_float("reg_alpha", 0.01, 10, log=True),
        "reg_lambda": trial.suggest_float("reg_lambda", 0.01, 10, log=True),
        "random_state": 42,
        "n_jobs": -1,
        "verbosity": -1
    }
    model = LGBMRegressor(**params)
    model.fit(X_tr, y_tr)
    pred = np.clip(model.predict(X_val), 0, 20)
    return np.sqrt(mean_squared_error(y_val, pred))

lgbm_study = optuna.create_study(direction="minimize", sampler=TPESampler(seed=42))
lgbm_study.optimize(lgbm_objective, n_trials=50, show_progress_bar=True)

print(f"Best LightGBM params: {lgbm_study.best_params}")
print(f"Best Val RMSE: {lgbm_study.best_value:.4f}")

Ensemble (XGBoost + Random Forest + LightGBM)¶
Averaging predictions from the three best tree models often reduces variance and improves generalization.


















In [294]:






# Simple average ensemble of XGBoost, Random Forest, and LightGBM
y_pred_test_ensemble = np.clip((y_pred_test_xgb + y_pred_test_rf + y_pred_test_lgbm) / 3, 0, 20)
y_pred_train_ensemble = np.clip((y_pred_train_xgb + y_pred_train_rf + y_pred_train_lgbm) / 3, 0, 20)

rmse_ensemble = np.sqrt(mean_squared_error(y_train, y_pred_train_ensemble))

print(f"Ensemble Train RMSE: {rmse_ensemble:.4f}")
print(f"XGBoost Train RMSE:  {rmse_xgb:.4f}")
print(f"RF Train RMSE:       {rmse_rf:.4f}")
print(f"LightGBM Train RMSE: {rmse_lgbm:.4f}")
print(f"\nEnsemble test predictions: mean={y_pred_test_ensemble.mean():.3f}, std={y_pred_test_ensemble.std():.3f}")

Create Submission¶
Creating submission file using the best performing model (based on training RMSE).


















In [295]:






# Store all predictions
all_predictions = {
    "linear": y_pred_test_lr,
    "ridge": y_pred_test_ridge,
    "lasso": y_pred_test_lasso,
    "random_forest": y_pred_test_rf,
    "xgboost": y_pred_test_xgb,
    "lightgbm": y_pred_test_lgbm,
    "ensemble": y_pred_test_ensemble
}

# Create submission file for each model
for name, pred in all_predictions.items():
    submission = pd.DataFrame({
        "ID": test_df["ID"],
        "item_cnt_month": pred
    })
    submission.to_csv(f"submission_{name}.csv", index=False)
    print(f"submission_{name}.csv: mean={pred.mean():.3f}")

# Also save best model as submission.csv
best_model_name = results_df.iloc[0]["Model"]
best_key = best_model_name.lower().replace(" ", "_")
best_pred = all_predictions[best_key]

submission = pd.DataFrame({
    "ID": test_df["ID"],
    "item_cnt_month": best_pred
})
submission.to_csv("submission.csv", index=False)

print(f"\n✓ Best model ({best_model_name}) saved as submission.csv")

print(submission.head(10))
